evidence_proposition: The repository SplitMix64 stream and Box-Muller sampler reproduce the moments, bin counts, tail counts and chi-square and Kolmogorov statistics re-derived by the retained stdlib generator, and the stored screening p-values meet the pinned thresholds.
limitations: The stream conventions are restated, not derived; the checks are exact reproduction of one stream per seed (20000 draws each) plus screening bands on p-values, not a test of randomness quality. The Kolmogorov p-values use the asymptotic law and agree with the stored SciPy values to about 1 percent. The normaltest statistic and p-value are stored but not recomputed here and are read from the fixture by the test. Uniform bin and pair chi-squares and the uniform Kolmogorov distance are recomputed from the product stream in the test; the normal Kolmogorov distance, skew and kurtosis are not asserted against the product. Calibration unmeasured.

oracle.project: stdlib SplitMix64 and Box-Muller re-derivation with exact integer stream arithmetic
oracle.historical_exposure: The original NumPy/SciPy harness was not retained. This replacement was written during this review from the published SplitMix64 and Box-Muller definitions and the fixture's stated stream conventions; it reproduces every stored stream statistic to 1e-12. No product statistical routine was consulted, though the seed offset, 53-bit mapping and u1 floor conventions were read from the repository stream to state them.
oracle.method: published SplitMix64 and Box-Muller definitions reimplemented in Python integers and stdlib math
oracle.independence_basis: The generator rebuilds the SplitMix64 stream from the published definition (golden-ratio increment and the two xor-shift-multiply rounds), starts it at seed XOR gamma, maps the top 53 bits to a uniform and forms Box-Muller (cos, sin) pairs with u1 floored at 2^-53, using only integer arithmetic and the stdlib math module. It recomputes the moments, lag-1 correlation, 20-bin counts, 10x10 pair table chi-square, tail counts, skew, excess kurtosis and both Kolmogorov distances, plus chi-square and Kolmogorov p-values from its own special functions. It imports no Antecedent code, NumPy or SciPy. The seed-to-state offset, the 53-bit mapping, the pair order and the u1 floor are conventions of the repository stream stated in the fixture, shared with the product; SplitMix64 itself is a published algorithm.
oracle.generation_location: conformance/stats/rng_gaussian/reference.py (retained; the original SciPy harness is recorded in historical_reference)
asserted_outputs: uniform mean, population variance, lag-1 correlation, 20-bin counts, bin and pair chi-squares, Kolmogorov distance
normal mean, population variance and absolute tail counts
context_only_outputs: all p-values and the normaltest statistic (read by the test as threshold checks)
normal skew, excess kurtosis and Kolmogorov distance
